The second is thicker than the first, often almost solid, procured from the combs by preflure : and the worst is the common yellow honey, extra&ed by heating the combs over the fire, and then prefling them. In the flowers of plants, by certain glands near the basis in the petals, is secreted a sweet juice, which the bee, by means of its proboscis or trunk, sucks, up, swallows it, flies away with it to the hive, and discharges again from the stomach through the mouth into some of the cells of the comb.
